paragraphs.text: Cyrus: He was born in Elam and became king there in 558 BC. He was able to conquer Media in 549 BC, then Persia in 548 BC and Babylon in 538 BC. Because of the importance of Persia he was called the king of Persia. He was courageous, gentle in his feelings and religiously tolerant, so he allowed the inhabitants of his kingdom each to worship his own god. In the first year of his reign, after his victory over Babylon, the events of this book began.

After the Jews had spent seventy years in the Babylonian captivity, the kingdom of Media and Persia was able to defeat Babylon, and its first king, Cyrus, made a proclamation by word of mouth and in writing throughout his whole kingdom, calling the Jews to return to Jerusalem. He kept a copy of these orders in the records of the royal palace, and these are the ones whose importance appeared in the days of Darius the king (Ezra 6:1). For Daniel and the elders of the Jews had shown King Cyrus that his name was written in the books of their prophets Isaiah and Jeremiah (Isa 44:28; Jer 25:12; 29:10), and that they had prophesied that Cyrus would bring the Jews back from captivity so that they might build the temple and Jerusalem. The king was greatly pleased that his name had been written in the books of the prophets for more than two centuries, and he believed in God, the God of heaven, as one of the gods. He took an interest in the return of the Jews to build the house of God, and to ask on behalf of the stability of his kingdom. It is to be noted that Isaiah prophesied the return from captivity before Jeremiah prophesied the destruction of Jerusalem and the captivity, for God gives hope to His children before the affliction.

History tells us that Cyrus took care to set up temples for the gods throughout his kingdom, to gain their favor and to secure the loyalty of the peoples to him, so that they would not rise in revolt against him. But God had put this in his heart so that His people might return to worship Him in Jerusalem.

The proclamation was made throughout the whole kingdom of Media and Persia so that it would reach all the scattered Jews, whom Assyria or Babylon had taken captive, that they might return to Jerusalem.

Cyrus felt that his victories and the expansion of his kingdom had come through the help of God, the God of heaven. God called him His anointed and commanded him to build a house for Him in Jerusalem, as the prophets had prophesied.

Cyrus sensed that God, the God of heaven, was the cause of his victories and of his taking the kingdoms of the earth. He believed in Him as a god, and this made him ready to carry out God's commandment to him to build a temple for the Lord in Jerusalem. Here one opinion holds that God appeared to him in a dream, confirming what the prophets had written, which made him say that God had charged him.

Cyrus called every one of God's people who wished to return to Jerusalem to build the temple of God, and he encouraged him that God would be with him. This is great faith and an encouragement to obey God and believe in Him. It is strange that such a feeling should come from a pagan, while it is not found in the hearts of many of God's people, who did not return from Jerusalem and preferred their material attachments in captivity.

It is beautiful that Cyrus did not force anyone to return, although he had the authority to do so, but gave them freedom, because the true worship of God is accomplished only by man's choice and his love for God. Cyrus told those returning to Jerusalem that they would go up to it, for it is built upon five hills. This signifies that the temple of God is higher than the world, and that the spiritual life requires man to rise above his material attachments in order to enter it and enjoy it.

Cyrus called Him the God of Israel because after the captivity the division between the two kingdoms of Israel disappeared and they became one kingdom. Affliction helps people give up their divisions and live in the unity of love.

Cyrus required everyone who had remained in his faith in the God of Israel and his love for rebuilding His temple, wherever his place of exile might be in the kingdom of Media and Persia, to take from those around him, whether Jews or pagans, gifts for the building and service of the temple while he was traveling to Jerusalem. He also required all the people subject to him to hasten in giving to him, saying, "let them help", because the returning Jew had no money for building the temple. In this way Cyrus supplied the expenses of building the temple from the contributions of his people. He not only permitted them, but required his people to contribute, because Cyrus cared about the building of the temple and the satisfaction of the God of heaven with him.

By this the promise of God was fulfilled, which He promised to His people by the mouth of Isaiah the prophet (Isa 10:21; 40:9; 11:11), that the remnant of the children of Israel, who would be humbled by captivity, would be saved and return to Jerusalem. For this reason Isaiah called his son "Shearjashub", that is, "a remnant shall be saved" (Isa 7:3). These gifts were among the most precious things a man can possess, namely silver and gold, then cattle and any other contributions. Cyrus required his people to give the most precious of what they had for the completion of the building of the temple in Jerusalem. It is impossible to imagine that these things could happen unless God was behind all this, and it was He who moved the heart of Cyrus to carry out His will.

These contributions and gifts resemble what the Egyptians did for the children of Israel when they went out of Egypt, but the Egyptians' gifts were given out of fear of the God of Israel, whereas here they are offerings of love for the great God, especially since the Jews were loved by the Babylonians among whom they had lived. The giving of the pagans together with the Jews for the temple of God was like the sharing of Jews and pagans in building the temple of Solomon, and all this is a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, which atones for believers of Jewish origin and of Gentile origin alike.

This verse also shows the importance of cooperation. Whoever cannot go to Jerusalem should at least contribute to show his feelings toward God, for team spirit is of great benefit in accomplishing successful works.
Giving to build or renew the house of God is love and honor for Him. Do not let this opportunity pass you by, so that you may show your love for Him and enjoy His presence in the Church.

entries.section: (3) The return of the vessels of the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: We see God's care in preserving the vessels of His house for seventy years, although they could have been melted down and turned into ingots of silver and gold for the Babylonians to use. They had destroyed everything that remained in the temple of God, and they took the vessels as material objects of high value, because they were of silver and gold.

The intention of Cyrus to honor God and build His house appears in the fact that he did not only proclaim the return of his people to Jerusalem, but supported them by giving them the vessels of the house of their God.
Cyrus' giving of these vessels to God's people was one of the incentives for them to hasten their return to Jerusalem, to build the temple of God and to use its vessels in worship.

entries.section: (3) The return of the vessels of the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Cyrus commanded the one in charge of his treasures, Mithredath, to hand over all the vessels of the house of the Lord to Sheshbazzar, who is Zerubbabel, after he had appointed him governor of Jerusalem and Judea. So he counted the vessels and handed them over to Zerubbabel.

The verse mentions that Sheshbazzar is the prince of Judah, and Haggai (Hag 1:1) mentions that Zerubbabel is the governor of Judah, which means that Sheshbazzar is a Persian name for Zerubbabel. Sheshbazzar is a Persian word meaning joy in the midst of troubles, "whereas Zerubbabel is a Hebrew word meaning "seed of Babylon" or "born in Babylon." Ezra mentions that "Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel" (Ezra 3:2), but in 1 Chronicles 3:9 he calls him "Zerubbabel the son of Pedaiah". This is because Shealtiel was the eldest son of King Jehoiachin and Shealtiel had no children, so his younger brother Pedaiah married his wife, according to the Law (Deut 25:5, 6), and begot Zerubbabel. Thus Zerubbabel is the son of Shealtiel according to the Law, and at the same time the son of Pedaiah according to the flesh.

Jehoiachin lived a long time after the captivity in Babylon, and Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel or Pedaiah as we have mentioned, is his grandson. From this it is understood that he held a standing among his people because he was of the royal line, and perhaps for this reason Cyrus chose him to be governor over Judah.

Among the reasons that may have led Cyrus to return the vessels of the house of the Lord to his people returning to Jerusalem is that he had heard that Belshazzar, the last of the Babylonian kings, had sinned by drinking wine from the vessels of the house of the Lord, and died that same night, and Cyrus entered and took the city. So Cyrus feared God and returned the vessels of His house to His people.

entries.section: (3) The return of the vessels of the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Here the numbers of the vessels of the house of the Lord are mentioned, and we notice that the numbers mentioned add up to less than the total stated in (v. 11). This is because the number given in (vv. 9, 10) is of the large vessels, and the rest are the small vessels, or those that were broken because of being transported. This shows God's care for every vessel of His house, since these vessels signify His people, each one a member of His Church, and He cares for him however small he may be. If the vessels of the house of the Lord were taken into captivity and remained for many years, God has returned them to Jerusalem with honor, and He is also able to bring back His children however far they have strayed from Him, even if they have been defiled by evil. He is able to cleanse them and restore them to their first rank as living members in His house.

You are a member in the body of Christ as long as you are bound to the Holy Sacraments and the means of grace. So do not stumble because of your weakness or your sins and say that God has forgotten me, or does not hear my prayer. God cares for you and gives the small members a great standing in His Kingdom if they are faithful in their love for God and hold fast to Him. Those who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel

The seventh month is a month that includes many feasts. On its first day is the Feast of Shouting, that is, the Feast of Trumpets (Num 29:1); on its tenth is the Day of Atonement (Num 29:7); and on its fifteenth is the Feast of Tabernacles (Num 29:12). It is beautiful that the people paid attention and came to Jerusalem at the beginning of the seventh month, that is, on the day of the Feast of Trumpets, to attend to the building of the altar of God.

We see unity in the gathering of the children of Israel with one heart, that is, as one man, to build the altar of God. They were men and women, rich and poor, great and small, and their gathering had a great purpose, namely the worship of God. The length of the period between the arrival of the children of Israel in their cities and their gathering in Jerusalem is not known exactly, but it seems to have been a short period. For if they set out from Babylon in the spring, which is a suitable time for travel, which takes about three months, and the seventh month begins approximately in the second half of September, then the short period they spent in their cities does not exceed three months. This shows that the first purpose of their return from captivity was the worship of God in His temple.

The name of Jeshua the high priest is mentioned before Zerubbabel, and he was the first high priest after the captivity, because the building of the altar is a priestly work according to the details of the Law. But at the building of the temple by order of King Cyrus, the name of Zerubbabel, the Persian governor, comes first, preceding the name of Jeshua in (v. 8). Sacrifices were offered from time to time on the remains of the ruined altar after the destruction of the temple, as is mentioned in (Jer 41:1-8), but now they were restoring and preparing the altar carefully according to the text of the Law. The priests and the people began by building the bronze altar first, before the rest of the details of the temple, because by the bronze altar sacrifices can be offered and worship and religious celebrations can begin; in addition, the surrounding peoples might oppose them if they undertook the great work of building the temple, as will appear after this. Here we find the importance of spiritual leadership in the person of Jeshua and the priests, and we also find the people's obedience to them in building the altar. All this shows the strong spiritual inclination in the hearts of those returning from captivity. We see that Jeshua the high priest was the grandson of Seraiah, the last high priest before the captivity, whom Nebuchadnezzar killed when he burned the temple (2 Kgs 25:18-21). As for Zerubbabel, the civil governor of Jerusalem, he was of the line of David and one of the forefathers of Christ (Mt 1:12, 13). The beginning with the building of the altar, then the temple, signifies what Christ did when He began by offering the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross, and after this established His Church, which is founded upon the sacrifice.

It appears from this verse that the surrounding peoples were strong, so the children of Israel feared them, but they relied on the power of God, who made their return easy by the order of Cyrus. They set up the altar so that they might offer sacrifices upon it, and that it might be a support to them in completing the building of the temple, defending them before their enemies. In addition to this, the people felt that the altar was the divine power that had supported the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Likewise, it is possible to worship at an altar before a temple is completed, but it is not possible to worship in a temple without an altar.

Besides this, the building of the temple takes a long time, whereas the building of the altar can be completed quickly. Perhaps their fear of the enemies led them to complete the easiest step, which is the building of the altar, so that they would not oppose them in the building of the temple. This indeed happened, as will appear from the following chapters. The care of the priests appears in their setting up the altar in its exact place, and this required removing stones and repairing what was ruined, so that the altar would be in its proper form.
The building of the altar proclaims two things in the heart of the people:
1- The people's acknowledgment of their need to repent of their sins.
2- Their faith in the forgiving power of God.

How closely are you bound to the altar? It is the greatest place in the world, where Christ gives His Body and Blood. Let your heart and your life be bound to the altar, so that you may find your satisfaction and your strength and live in peace all your days.

entries.section: (2) The return of the religious seasons

paragraphs.text: It appears from (v. 6), as will come, that they kept the Feast of Trumpets, which is called the Feast of Shouting, by offering a burnt offering in it, and it falls on the first day of the seventh month. This feast is followed in the same month by the Day of Atonement, which falls on the tenth day, but they were not able to keep it, because on this feast the high priest must enter with the blood of the sacrifice into the Holy of Holies, which had not yet been built.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month falls the Feast of Tabernacles, and they were able to keep it as it is written in the Law of Moses, that is, as it is prescribed, in which they offer during the seven days of the feast a set number of sacrifices that decreases gradually until the seventh day (Num 29:13, 17). This is what is meant in the text of this verse by the expression "the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required." The rest of the rite of the feast is that they dwell in booths they make of tree branches, whether in the courtyards or on the roofs of the houses, and the eighth day is a day of solemn assembly.

The keeping of the Feast of Tabernacles after the people's return from captivity, together with the building of the new altar, reminds the people (1 Kgs 8:2) that they kept the Feast of Tabernacles at the beginning of the founding of the temple of Solomon.

The Feast of Tabernacles reminds the people of being strangers to the world and of clinging to God. This is a necessary matter that God wanted to confirm within the hearts of His people returning from captivity, that their goal in life is His worship, so that they would not be occupied with possessions and property. They did sin after this and became occupied with building their own houses, but God sent them two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, who brought them back to caring about the building of the house of God and worship in it, as will appear in this book (Ezra 5:1).

entries.section: (2) The return of the religious seasons

paragraphs.text: The new moons: the beginnings of the months, on which they kept feasts.

After setting up the altar, the Jews began to carry out the Law, so they offered a morning burnt offering, then an evening burnt offering every day. In this way the fire remains burning on the altar continually, and that is a type of the sacrifice of Christ on the Cross, which is a perpetual atonement for those who believe in Him.

The Second Book of Maccabees (2 Macc 1:19-22) tells us that the Jews had hidden the sacred fire in a well in the days of Jeremiah, at the attack on Jerusalem. The elders who knew about this matter went and found that the fire had gone out, but they found water in the well. They took some of the holy water and put it on the burnt offering, and the sacred fire blazed up in the sacrifice on the altar.

Those returning from captivity began to celebrate the new moons and to offer sacrifices, and likewise at the religious seasons and feasts they carried out the rites and received the freewill contributions of the people offered in thanksgiving to God. Thus the service and worship returned to the temple of God.

entries.section: (2) The return of the religious seasons

paragraphs.text: Thus the service and the offering of sacrifices began as soon as the altar was built, which was built quickly on the first day of the seventh month.

But there is a possibility that some of the Jews had built the altar a month, or two, or more before the beginning of the seventh month, and then the Jews gathered from their cities at the beginning of the seventh month, kept the Feast of Shouting and offered the burnt offerings.

Take care to take part in the holy feasts and all the occasions of the Church, so that you may be rid of your spiritual lukewarmness, your heart may be bound to heavenly things, and you may grow in your love for God. For spiritual occasions are an opportunity to pay attention amid the crowd of life's concerns.
The masons: They are those who cut the stones from the mountain, that is, who hew them from the mountain and shape them into the form suitable for building.
The Sidonians: They are the inhabitants of Sidon, a coastal city in present-day Lebanon, which was famous for shipbuilding and fishing.
The sea of Joppa: Joppa is a Jewish coastal city on the Mediterranean Sea, which in this region is called the sea of Joppa.

The Jews set about their preparations for building the temple, and with the permission of King Cyrus they began their commercial negotiations with the Sidonians, who were not subject to the Persian kingdom. They agreed with them to send the timber from Sidon to Joppa, in return for giving them silver, and food, drink and oil for the Sidonian workmen who cut the wood, as Solomon had done long ago when building the temple of the Lord (1 Kgs 5:10, 11). Silver signifies redemption. The Jews paid silver to the Gentiles so that they would bring the wood for building the temple, and this signifies that redemption came out of the Jews for the salvation of the whole world, for Jews and Gentiles, for in the temple of God both Jews and Gentiles share in the work.

The silver was collected from the Jews returning from captivity. Despite their poverty they gave the most precious of their possessions out of love for God, His worship and the setting up of His temple, in addition to the silver they collected from their loved ones who were around them in captivity, as their support for the building of the temple, as Cyrus had commanded (ch. 1:4).
To set forward: to oversee the work and supervise it.
The importing of the timber from Sidon took several months, which is the period from the seventh month in the first year until the second month in the second year of their return to Jerusalem.

It is noticeable that Solomon finished building his temple in the second month (1 Kgs 6:1), and Zerubbabel begins the rebuilding of the temple in the second month, so he completes what Solomon began, regarding the period of captivity as an incidental period that passed over the Jews as a discipline for them, while their heart was attached to the temple which they had begun to build. The name of Zerubbabel the governor comes before Jeshua the high priest at the building of the temple, because Zerubbabel was commissioned by Cyrus to build the temple, and Jeshua, who understood the details of the rites of building the temple, helped him. Zerubbabel and Jeshua set up a careful system for supervising the building of the temple, so they arranged companies of the Levites to oversee the work, so that it would be accomplished according to the prescribed rites.

The age of the Levites who began the service was thirty years, and they continued until fifty years (Num 4:3), but in cases of necessity they could begin from the age of twenty, with no maximum age if their health allowed them to bear the hardships of the work (1 Chr 23:24, 27). Henadad, one of the heads among the Levites, is not mentioned in the second chapter of this book, and this is because he may have been at that time in Jerusalem and Judea and did not go into captivity. The Levites stood to oversee the work on the house of God, that is, in the place where the house would be built, because the house of God had not yet been built.

The people rejoiced when the foundations of the temple were laid and celebrated it. The priests put on the garments of service, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, who were in charge of the praise, took their cymbals, as David the prophet had arranged for them, and the trumpet of the priests. Then the sons of Asaph began to praise God, declaring their thanks to God whose mercy endures forever, because He had had compassion on His people and had granted them to re-found their temple and have their worship accepted by Him, after a captivity that lasted seventy years. The blowing of trumpets proclaims joy and gladness, and it took place at the Feast of Trumpets and at war (Num 10:8), seeking the help of God. Here, as an exceptional case, the priests used the trumpets in joy at the founding of the temple and in seeking the help of God, so that they might be able to complete its building if the surrounding Gentiles opposed them, as will appear in the next chapter. Strong feelings filled their hearts, namely:
1- Holy zeal and love for God whom they worship.
2- Their joy at fulfilling the will of God and the orders of their king Cyrus.
3- Their pride in belonging to the mighty God after having endured seventy years of humiliation.
When the elders among the priests and Levites and the heads of the fathers of the people saw the temple founded, they wept with a loud voice, for the following reasons:
1- They rejoiced at the re-founding of the temple of God which they had seen long ago before it was burned by Nebuchadnezzar.
2- Perhaps they remembered their sins that had brought the captivity upon them, but the mercy of God brought them back from captivity and they began to found the temple.
3- Perhaps they felt that this house was very modest compared with the great temple of Solomon, which they had lost because of their sins, so they felt grief over the temple of Solomon that was lost.
The mingling of these feelings calls for weeping, as the feelings of joy within the prodigal son at returning to his father mingled with feelings of sorrow over his sins.
The shout of the people rose in joy at the founding of the temple, and the shouting mingled with the sound of weeping, so that the voices were heard from afar.
Your true joy is in being with God, so take care to found a house for Him within you by prayers, meditations and praise, that you may remain in joy.
The opposition of the enemies and the stopping of the building

The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, who lived near them, heard that they had founded the temple and were trying to complete its building. They feared for themselves lest the Jews gain power and drive them out of their land or do them harm. So they made plans and plots to stop the building of the temple and to limit the strength of those returning from captivity.

These enemies were the remnants of the ten tribes of Israel who lived in Samaria and its surroundings and mixed with the pagans whom the Assyrians had transferred and settled in the region of Samaria. These moved during the period of the Babylonian captivity and settled north of Jerusalem on the border of the kingdom of Judah, since the land was empty and its inhabitants were few.

The creed of these Samaritans was a mixture of the worship of God and belief in the books of Moses with the worship of the two golden calves, that is, the idols that Jeroboam the son of Nebat set up after the split from the tribe of Judah and Jerusalem. To this was added the worship of the pagan gods of the pagans living with them, and we find their story in (2 Kgs 17). Therefore they were more dangerous to the people of God than the pagans, since they had the appearance of being Jews and worshiping God, although in truth they worshiped God as one of the gods and worshiped with Him the rest of the gods of the nations. Here the Jews are spoken of as the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, because most of those returning were from Judah and Benjamin and were able to prove their genealogies, whereas the rest of the tribes had been scattered and had forgotten their genealogies.

Esarhaddon: an Assyrian king who reigned from 681 to 669 BC. His policy was to remove the original inhabitants of a land and settle them in other places throughout his kingdom, in order to wipe out the nationality of these inhabitants so that they would all be citizens of the Assyrian kingdom, thus securing their submission. Accordingly he transferred pagans to the land of Samaria, and they mixed with the Jews who had split off from the tribe of Judah, that is, the ten tribes, and they worshiped God along with them together with the rest of the pagan gods.

The Samaritans who lived near Jerusalem came forward and asked Zerubbabel and the elders of Judah to let them share with them in building the house of God, whom their fathers had worshiped since the days of Esarhaddon's transfer of them from their lands to the region of Samaria. They declared that they were Jews, like the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and therefore they had the right to build the house of the Lord. This was deceit and a means of stopping the building of the temple, because they worshiped God as one of the gods, did not keep the rites of His worship, and wished to place the statues of their pagan gods beside Him in His temple, and if those returning from captivity resisted them, they would stop the building.

The deceit and pride of these Samaritans appeared when those returning from captivity refused to let them share in the building, so they opposed them openly, as in the following verses. Thus the malice and evil of their hearts appeared, and in this they are like Judas Iscariot, about whom the Psalm prophesied (Ps 55:21).

Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the elders of Israel answered with one heart and in a decisive decision, and said to the Samaritans that the order of King Cyrus was for us alone, that we might build the house of the Lord, so it is not right for you to share with us in building it. God had revealed to them the deceit and trickery of the enemies, and they understood that they were not Jews like them, worshiping God alone. In this they showed that there is no fellowship of righteousness with iniquity, or of the people of God with the pagans.

After the people of God refused to let the pagans, the people of the land, that is, the Samaritans, share with them in the building, they showed their evil toward the people of God and began a series of plots to stop the building, for they knew that it was easier for them to stop the building from within than to stop it by an armed attack or by a royal order. Among these plots were:
1- An attempt to weaken the resolve of the Jews, so that they would grow lazy about building the house of God and be distracted from its worship.

2- When the attempt to make the people of God grow lazy about building failed, they resorted to a second means, which was to frighten the Jews, that is, to spread panic and terror in their hearts, whether by saying that the nations would rise against them, or that the king would be angry with them, or that wild beasts would attack them... But by the grace of God His people remained firm in faith and completed the building of the temple.

3- Finally they resorted to a third means, which was to hire counselors within the royal court of King Cyrus, hoping to find a pretext or a reason to stop the building, and they paid many bribes. But the attempts of these counselors failed throughout the reign of Cyrus, and they continued these bribes to the counselors of the Persian king, not only in the days of Cyrus but also in the days of his son Cambyses, who is also called Artaxerxes, and until the reign of Darius, who reigned in 521 BC. Unfortunately Cambyses (Artaxerxes) responded to the wicked counselors, but Darius did not respond to them (you may consult the chronological table of the kings of Persia found in the introduction to this book).

Be firm in your faith however much the plots of the wicked surround you, and God will not allow any harm to come to you except what benefits you, and He will be with you and support you. Be confident and assured that your God, the Almighty, will never leave you.

The enemies of the people of God also resorted to official complaints which they sent to the kings of Persia. They may have begun in the days of Cyrus, but he did not respond to them, and they continued after this for a long time; that is, they sent them to many of the kings of Persia, even sending a complaint in the days of Ahasuerus, who reigned later, between 486 and 465 BC, and who married Esther. But they were not able to submit complaints to the king after him, Artaxerxes Longimanus, because he loved the Jews and appointed Nehemiah as his cupbearer, and in his days he allowed Ezra to return to Jerusalem, followed by Nehemiah in the third return. All this shows how evil these enemies were, who were able at a certain time to stop the building of the temple, as we shall see in the following verses. And even after the Jews were able to complete the building of the temple in the days of Darius, they afterward resumed sending complaints, even in the days of Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther.

The word for complaint in the Hebrew language is "sitnah", from which the word "Satan" or the devil is taken, who is the accuser of the children of God. That is, these wicked men walked in the way of Satan to hinder the work of God. But God is stronger than they.

Ezra tells us of one of the complaints that were sent in the days of King Artaxerxes, who is also called Cambyses, the son of Cyrus, who reigned from 529 to 522 BC. This complaint was presented by three of the chiefs of the nations surrounding the people of God, and King Artaxerxes was influenced by it. The text of this letter is not mentioned in the Bible, like the complaint of Ahasuerus mentioned in (v. 6) and like the rest of the complaints that were sent to King Cyrus.

The letter of Bishlam and his companions was written in the Aramaic language and interpreted in Aramaic, that is, written in Aramaic letters and not in Persian letters or any other language. Ezra did not translate these letters from Aramaic into Hebrew, but wrote them as they were, and this shows Ezra's accuracy. The written texts of the complaints and letters in this chapter, up to the sixth chapter, are all written in the Aramaic language.

This is a new complaint written by a person well known among the nations named Rehum, whose office was chancellor, that is, the judge or governor on behalf of the Persian state of a region neighboring Jerusalem and Judea, and he was assisted by his scribe Shimshai.
Rehum wrote this complaint also to Artaxerxes, that is, King Cambyses.

Asnapper: He was most likely Ashurbanipal, one of the kings of Assyria, a powerful king who transferred many peoples from their lands to other lands, among them the region of Samaria, which lies north of Jerusalem, and he reigned from 668 to 626 BC. This complaint was sent by Rehum and Shimshai, mentioned previously in (v. 8), and a great number of the peoples living in the region of Samaria, who had been transferred from distant lands in the kingdom of Assyria, allied themselves with them, so their names were written after the name of Rehum at the beginning of this letter. This was to show the importance and gravity of the complaint, that many had agreed upon it or signed it, and this also shows how evil these enemies were and their attempt to stir up King Artaxerxes against the Jews. Then they completed the rest of the usual introduction in glorifying kings, saying "and so forth."

Rehum and his companions showed their submission to King Artaxerxes in their complaint and made it known to him that they were his servants living in the region beyond the river, that is, the region lying west of the Euphrates river, which includes the region of present-day Syria and Palestine as far as the Mediterranean.
The complaint contained false accusations and left out important facts, in order to make Jerusalem appear in a bad light, and it included the following:

1- The enemies accused the Jews who had gone up from Babylon to Jerusalem of building Jerusalem, the rebellious city, although it was a city subject to kings; but they exploited the rebellion of the last king of Judah, King Zedekiah, against Nebuchadnezzar (2 Chr 36:13), so Nebuchadnezzar seized him, took Jerusalem and destroyed it.

2- They also accused the Jews of building the wall of Jerusalem and repairing the foundations of the city, and this did not happen until many years later in the days of Nehemiah, and it was by order of another king.
3- They ignored the order of Cyrus, who asked Zerubbabel and the Jews with him to return and build the temple in Jerusalem.

4- They claimed that the Jews would rebel against the king if they completed the walls, and would not pay tribute, which is the taxes collected from the citizens of the Persian state, nor custom, which is the tax collected on lands, nor toll, which is the tax collected for the Persian governor. All this accusation was false, for the Jews never rebelled against the Persian kings, even after the building of the temple and the walls of Jerusalem.

The enemies of the Jews showed their love and submission to the king by saying "we have maintenance from the king's palace", which means the king's favor to them, for he feeds them, since they receive their allowances from the king. So they showed their loyalty to the king and that they could not bear any harm coming upon the king. All this was of course lies, for they were wicked and did not want the greatness and strength of the Jews, fearing them, so they flattered the king to turn his heart against the Jews.
Thus we see in this chapter a series of steps in evil which these enemies took, namely:
1- Deceit, by claiming that they wanted to help the Jews in the building (v. 2).
2- Weakening the resolve of the people (v. 4).
3- Frightening the people so that they would not complete the building (v. 4).
4- Paying bribes to the counselors of the king of Persia so that they would speak evil of the Jews to the king (v. 5).
5- Submitting complaints directly against the Jews (vv. 6-8).
6- Flattering the king and showing their loyalty to him in order to stir him up against the Jews (v. 14).
7- False accusations against the Jews, gathering any old faults of theirs, even from hundreds of years ago, calling Jerusalem the rebellious city (v. 15).
8- Exploiting the Persians' love of collecting taxes to support their armies, by frightening them that if the Jews completed the building they would not pay taxes (v. 16).
The book of the records of thy fathers: the accounts of the kings and the events that accompanied them were written down in books kept in the government or in the palaces of the kings.

They accused the Jews of rebellion, relying on the rebellion of some kings such as King Manasseh, Ahaz, Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, although the Jews returning from captivity were in complete submission to the state. Jerusalem had been destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, but the Jews did not present a harm to the state in general in their ancient generations, or in the recent generations, that is, after the return from captivity, when they were in utmost submission.
They threatened the king that when the building of Jerusalem and its walls was completed, it would certainly refuse to pay taxes, although this was a lie and did not happen.
Satan always stirs up the wicked to flatter and fawn upon rulers and to accuse the innocent falsely, as happened with Christ and happens to this day with the children of God.

Accept the false accusations and seek the counsel of God, and He will defend you. Know that Christ your Lord endured many false accusations for your sake, and be sure that He protects you and will make your right appear at the proper time.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: King Cambyses (Artaxerxes) answered the letter of Rehum and Shimshai and their companions with a message in which he first gave them peace, although the king's letter was full of evil against the Jews and in support of the evil of the Jews' enemies. The king had been drawn into the way of evil, but he offers peace as a customary word that does not carry its meaning.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The king said that the letter of Rehum had been plainly read before him, although Rehum had written it in Aramaic and then it was translated into Persian for the king to understand. He did not examine it carefully to know whether Rehum was harboring evil toward others or speaking with simplicity of heart. The king was deceived by the words of hypocrisy and praise that Rehum spoke, and he appears to understand everything while he understood nothing.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The king ordered his assistants to search the records kept by the king concerning the Jews, and they found, as he said, the following:
1- Jerusalem is a city that rebels against kings and revolts against them.
2- Mighty kings ruled over Jerusalem, who had their standing and whose power was feared.
3- The kings of Jerusalem were strong and paid great taxes to the empire, and therefore the submission of this city is important so that the empire may receive taxes from them.

We must notice the presence of wicked, bribed counselors working for the king. When they searched for the accounts of the Jews, they were certain to look for proofs that condemned the Jews, and they would of course hide the order of Cyrus, who had commanded the return of the Jews from captivity and the building of the temple.

The search of the ancient documents showed that the kings of Jerusalem paid taxes, and this is positive evidence in favor of Jerusalem. But the king, because his assistants had stirred him up against Jerusalem, considered this matter alarming, since it was possible that Jerusalem would refuse to pay taxes.

The king's assistants who searched gathered the complaints that Rehum had sent since the days of Cyrus, all of them false complaints and false accusations, and presented them to the king as documents against Jerusalem. This is the habit of Satan, to bring logical proofs for his claims against the children of God. But whoever prays and examines calmly discovers the truth.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The king ordered the building to be stopped, and in this he fell into the error of contradicting the order of Cyrus his father, though it is not right to cancel a royal order, for the law of kings is not repealed (Dan 6:8). But the mercy of God appears in the king's order to stop the building in the following:
1- The stopping was for a time until another order should be issued by the king, and was not a final stopping.
2- The king did not order the demolition of what had been built.
3- He did not punish those who had done the building, nor send them back into captivity.
God permitted the order to stop the building to be issued for the following reasons:

1- The heart of the Jews was not complete in caring for the building of the temple, as shown by their being occupied, after the building of the temple was stopped, with building their own houses, so God sent the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to alert the people to the importance of building the temple of God.

2- So that those returning from captivity might feel the importance of building the temple when its building was stopped, and then, after a period, it was permitted through the alert and prayers of those who love God. What comes easily is lost easily, but what a man obtains with labor he keeps with great care.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The weakness of King Artaxerxes appeared when he implored Rehum and those with him in his letter to carry out the order, so that no harm would come to him, especially since at the same time some skirmishes had broken out from the Greeks, whose aim was to seize some cities in Syria that were subject to his empire.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: Rehum and his companions rejoiced at the king's letter, which contained the stopping of the building of the temple, and hastened with forces of soldiers and stopped the building in Jerusalem and showed them the king's order. They carried out the order quickly because it agreed with their evil desire, and not out of love for the king.

entries.section: (3) The stopping of the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The building of the temple stopped as a result of the order of King Artaxerxes, and that was about the year 530 BC, and the stoppage continued until the second year of the reign of Darius, which is the year 520 BC, that is, it stopped for about ten years.

The Bible does not state that in this period the people grieved, prayed or fasted; rather they cared for building their own houses and were so occupied with them that they needed someone to awaken them spiritually, so God sent Haggai and Zechariah, who rebuked them for abandoning the building of the temple of God. It appears that the king's order stopped them, but the truth is that their heart was not concerned with completing the building of the temple. They had begun well when they set up the altar and laid the foundations of the temple, but they grew slack. So when the king's order to stop came, the Jews accepted it quietly because it agreed with their inward slackness. But when they were awakened spiritually, God bestowed on them not only the building of the temple but also its dedication, then the building of the walls of Jerusalem and their dedication, although this took time, so that their faith and steadfastness in God might be perfected. It was accomplished about seventy-five years after the year 520 BC, from the rebuilding of the temple until 445 BC at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

May you be with God with all your heart when you pray or do any good work, and if troubles come upon you, hold fast to your prayers, and the problem will be solved, and in any case your spiritual growth increases in both ease and distress. The return to the building of the temple

1- The building of the temple of God began by order of King Cyrus in 535 BC, one year after his return from captivity, and continued for five years until the death of Cyrus in 530 BC, and his son Artaxerxes (Cambyses) became king, to whom the enemies of the people of God were able to complain about the Jews, so he issued an order to stop the building. It stopped for about ten years, until 520 BC, which is the second year of King Darius.

2- We see in this chapter how the people grew slack and the Jews became occupied with building their own houses, so God sent them two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, who encouraged them, and they began building the temple, and God supported them, so the complaint of the civil governors of the region did not hinder them, as we shall see in this chapter.

entries.section: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The people grew slack and no longer had enthusiasm for building the house of the Lord, for the following reasons:
1- Their preoccupation with building their own private houses, and the rich among them cared for adorning them, so they paneled their houses on the inside (Hag 1:3).
2- The weakness of their spiritual inclination. They had begun with enthusiasm, but their resolve weakened until it almost vanished with regard to building the house of the Lord.

Because of the severe spiritual weakness of the people, God sent them two prophets, not one prophet, Haggai and Zechariah, as He had sent earlier Elijah and Elisha, then Isaiah and after him Jeremiah, and likewise Daniel and Ezekiel in the captivity. The prophecy of Haggai began several months before the prophecy of Zechariah, and the prophecies of Haggai were marked by rebuke for the Jews' building of their own houses and their neglect of building the house of the Lord, while the prophecy of Zechariah was marked by encouragement (Zech 4:6). Thus by this complementarity the spiritual benefit is complete and the people rise up.
The prophecy of Haggai is also characterized by direct speech, whereas Zechariah uses visions abundantly to bring the meaning near.

The grace of God supported the two prophets, so they spoke in the name of the Lord, and they had awe and a spiritual influence on the people because of the Lord's support for them, especially since all the people were in slackness; even the two leaders, Zerubbabel and Jeshua, had yielded to this weakness. So it was necessary for God to intervene to encourage His people to worship Him.

entries.section: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The people responded to the words of the two prophets, and under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua began the building of the temple of God, whose building had stopped for about ten years.

The beginning of the building did not make the two prophets slack, but they continued in their work of encouragement and rebuke until the people completed the building of the temple, and perhaps they, together with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, shared with the people by their own hands in the building, to encourage the people.

The leaders of the work were the governor, who was Zerubbabel, the high priest, who was Jeshua, and the two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, and the leader of our spiritual life is Christ, the King, Priest and Prophet.
Zerubbabel is a type of Christ in the following:
1- Zerubbabel brought the people of God back from captivity, and Christ freed us from the captivity of sin by His death on the Cross.

2- Zerubbabel founded the new temple after the captivity, and Christ founded the temple of the Church of the New Testament by the sacrifice of Himself on the Cross, despite the opposition of enemies to both.
3- Zerubbabel was of the tribe of Judah, and so was Christ.

entries.section: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: The Persian Empire comprised twenty provinces, one of which was the province beyond the river, which includes the region lying west of the Euphrates river, that is, Syria, Palestine and the surrounding areas. The governor of this province was a man named Tatnai, and he was assisted in this province by Shethar-boznai. Complaints reached Tatnai from some of the surrounding nations that the Jews were building a temple without permission, or perhaps the inspectors under Tatnai throughout his province reported this building to him.

Tatnai and Shethar-boznai and a group of their assistants came to Jerusalem to verify the matter, and they found that the building of the temple was indeed under way. Tatnai spoke with the governor Zerubbabel, who was considered his subordinate over Jerusalem and Judea, and asked him and those with him about the permit they had to carry out this building. Tatnai's question was an inquiry so that matters would proceed properly, and not out of enmity or opposition, as had happened earlier with Rehum in (ch. 4).

entries.section: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: Tatnai asked for the names of those carrying out the building, and Zerubbabel came forward boldly, wrote his name and the names of the chiefs who helped him in the building, and presented them to Tatnai. Here we see Tatnai's neutral integrity in keeping matters in order and knowing exactly what was going on in his province, and also the courage of Zerubbabel and all his helpers in the building, because God had encouraged them through the two prophets.

entries.section: (1) The two prophets and the building of the temple

paragraphs.text: God gave the Jews favor in the eyes of Tatnai, so he did not stop them from completing the building of the temple, but told them that he would send to King Darius to verify their words, because Zerubbabel told him, as we shall see in the following verses, that Cyrus had issued an order to them to build. By the grace of God Tatnai tried to help them, so he paid no heed to the order of Artaxerxes to stop the building and promised them that he would inform them of Darius' reply on this matter. Here we see the accuracy of Ezra the priest and scribe, who was able to obtain the texts of the letters sent to the kings of Persia, whether from Rehum, who was hostile to the Jews, or from Tatnai, who was friendly to the Jews, and perhaps Ezra obtained these texts from the government records while he was living in captivity, before he came to Jerusalem.

God's eye is upon you, watching over you and supporting you, so do not be troubled by the opposition of enemies, but seek Him and rely on Him and continue in your spiritual striving, confident of His support.

Tatnai sent a letter to King Darius, giving him greetings at its beginning, as is the custom of letters, and it was signed by him and Shethar-boznai and the Apharsachites, who were a group of his assistants in the administration of the province.

Tatnai informed King Darius that he had visited Jerusalem to examine the information that had reached him, and saw for himself the building that was going on there. It is noticeable that in his report Tatnai tried to persuade the king and encourage him to agree to the completion of the building, and this appears from the following:

1- He described the temple as the house of the great God. This means that God placed in Tatnai's heart reverence and fear of Him, for although he was a pagan who believed in many gods, he considered Him a great god among the gods.

2- He magnified the building by describing it as being built with great stones, although they were the fallen stones left from the ruins of the temple of Solomon, and they were indeed huge stones (2 Chr 22:2), but he did not describe them as fallen stones, but as great.

3- He declared to the king that the work was proceeding with speed and great success, to show the king the strength of the building and the blessing of this God who completes the building of His house and helps those who believe in Him.

The hand of God supports His children as long as they work faithfully and lovingly and in submission to His word, as the people submitted to the words of the two prophets. So be faithful in your work and service to God, and be sure that God will make you prosper and give you many blessings.

Tatnai informed Darius that when he examined what was being done in Jerusalem, he asked for the names of the chiefs responsible for the building, and wrote down all the names and sent them with this letter to the king, and this shows his accuracy and faithfulness; as he does his work faithfully, he also encourages the Jews. From Tatnai's question to the elders of Israel about who had commanded them to build the temple, it is understood that he had recently taken over the province beyond the river and did not know the order that had been issued by Cyrus in 536 BC, that is, sixteen years earlier.

Tatnai added that the elders of the Jews told him that they worship God, who is the God of heaven and earth. This is a magnification of God above the pagan gods, and although Tatnai says it on the tongue of the Jews, his informing Darius of it shows his esteem for God and for those who believe in Him.

The elders of the Jews also said that this house was built by a great king of theirs, meaning King Solomon, long ago, about 500 years before Darius, that is, about the year 1000 BC. This confirms the greatness of this house, that it was built by a great king and for a God who has no like, because He is the God of heaven and earth. The answer of the elders shows their courage and their faith in God when they said that He is the God of heaven and earth and were not afraid of the complaints of any of their enemies, because they had been strengthened by the word of God on the mouth of the two prophets.

The elders of the Jews confessed that they had sinned against their God and provoked Him to wrath, so He allowed Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to destroy this great house and take their fathers captive to the lands of the Babylonian kingdom. This is humility, repentance and acknowledgment of the truth on the part of the people of God.

The elders told Tatnai an important fact, which is that King Cyrus, the first of the kings of Persia, in the beginning of his reign, that is, in 538 BC, issued an order to rebuild this temple. That is, the order to build was issued from the beginning of the Persian Empire, and therefore the orders of kings are not repealed or turned back.

Tatnai added that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken the vessels of the house of the Lord, made of gold and silver, and carried them from Jerusalem to Babylon. After the fall of the Babylonian kingdom, Cyrus, the first of the kings of Media and Persia, became king and took these vessels from Babylon and gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, who is Zerubbabel, and made him governor of Jerusalem and Judea. Cyrus asked Sheshbazzar to build a house for the Lord in Jerusalem and to place these vessels in it.

From these two verses we see Tatnai's accuracy and his assurances that the Jews were building their temple by order of King Cyrus, and another proof of their truthfulness, that they had received the vessels of the house of their God from Cyrus, those which Nebuchadnezzar had seized and God had kept without harm until they returned to His house in Jerusalem. This also shows the power of God, who is able to preserve the vessels of His house and to move kings to carry out His will. We also find that Zerubbabel, that is, Sheshbazzar, is a person answerable before the Persian king; he does not act on his own, but holds a position dependent on the state and builds by order of the king. Thus Tatnai directs King Darius to the fact that Sheshbazzar, that is, Zerubbabel, is a person subject to the kingdom who carries out its orders and is not disobedient or rebellious, he and all who are with him, and this of course reassures the king and invites him to agree to and support the completion of the building of the temple.

Tatnai informed King Darius that Sheshbazzar had carried out the orders of King Cyrus and laid the foundation of the house of the Lord and was building in it, and the work on the building of the temple was still continuing. We notice in the words of Tatnai the following:
1- Zerubbabel, that is, Sheshbazzar, is an obedient person committed to carrying out the orders of the king.

2- He did not mention the period when the building was stopped, nor the complaints of Rehum and his companions, which continued for many years, nor how they stopped the building, so as not to confuse the king's mind, but considers that the building is proceeding in a natural way and only needs to be completed.
Tatnai concludes his letter with the following:
1- A search for the order of Cyrus kept in the treasuries of the kingdom that are in Babylon, to confirm the truthfulness of the Jews, and this shows that Tatnai was a neutral and precise man.

2- He did not ask King Darius to search for the complaints of Rehum or the order of Artaxerxes to stop the building, because he supports the Jews and wants their good and the building of their temple.

3- Babylon was one of the capitals of the kingdom of Media and Persia, in addition to the city of Shushan the palace; that is, Babylon had been the capital of the Babylonian kingdom and continued as one of the capitals of the kingdom of Media and Persia.
4- Tatnai declares his submission to King Darius and his waiting for his orders in this matter, so that he may carry it out. Darius and the completion of the house of the Lord

entries.section: (1) The finding of the order of Cyrus

paragraphs.text: Darius gave attention to the letter of Tatnai and ordered a search for the order of King Cyrus for the building of the temple of the Lord, and his order was strict, so they took care to examine all the documents in the house of the rolls, which is a building in which the records of the kings of Persia and the various government orders are kept, and it was in the city of Babylon, which was one of the capitals of the Persian kingdom.

In Darius' conduct we see an attitude that helps the Jews and is not against them. He responded to the letter of Tatnai and searched for the evidence that would support the work of the Jews in completing the building, and of course this was because of God's work in his heart, as He worked long ago in the heart of Cyrus and made him command the building of the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (1) The finding of the order of Cyrus

paragraphs.text: Achmetha: one of the capitals of the empire of Media and Persia, located in the region of Media and considered the summer resort of the kings, and called in Greek "Ecbatana."

The search for the order of Cyrus continued, and they did not find it in Babylon, and because Darius' order was strict, they searched also in the other capitals of the kingdom in which there were houses of the kings' records, so they went to Achmetha and searched carefully, and finally found this order of Cyrus. The finding of the order means a number of things:

1- The care of Darius and his assistants in searching everywhere for the order of Cyrus, because he was sympathetic to the Jews and wanted to support them in this matter, so he was not content with its not being found in Babylon and order the building to be stopped, but the search continued until they found it.
2- God's care in preserving this document after sixteen years, during which the document could have been lost or damaged.
3- The search continuing for a long time allowed the Jews to continue building the temple, and this was a grace from God to them.

entries.section: (1) The finding of the order of Cyrus

paragraphs.text: The assistants of Darius found the order of King Cyrus, and it contained the following:
1- It was issued in the first year of Cyrus' reign.
2- It concerns the building of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
3- It is to be built in the place of the old house of the Lord which was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar.

4- He allowed its dimensions to be sixty cubits in length and likewise sixty cubits in breadth, that is, that it should not exceed these dimensions, or should be within them, and he allows the Jews to build the house with the measurements they want, especially since the measurements of the temple of Solomon were less than what Cyrus allowed.

5- He allowed it not to exceed these dimensions, or to be within the limits of these dimensions, and he allows the Jews to build the house with the measurements they want, especially since the measurements of the temple of Solomon were less than what Cyrus allowed.

6- He specified the building materials, which were great stones and new timber, and this shows the care of King Cyrus for the building of a house of greater standing, and at the same time it supports the Jews who were building with great stones, as Tatnai saw and explained in his letter to Darius, that they were carrying out the order of Cyrus and were doing nothing for which anyone could call them to account.

7- He also specified the manner of building, which was to build the stones in three rows, then a row of timber, and so on, that is, repeating this throughout the building, so that it would be strong and firmly bonded.
8- The funding of the building of the house of the Lord was to be at the king's expense.

9- The return of the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and brought to Babylon, so that these vessels would be returned to Jerusalem and placed in the house of the Lord for its service.

Now in this chapter we see that the details of the order of Cyrus the great king, which were not mentioned before, show the extent of his sympathy and care for the building of the house of the Lord, such as the dimensions of the house, the type of building materials and the manner of building.
God is ready to support you with many proofs and helps if your heart believes in Him and relies on Him and you do His will. He is with you and defends you in all that you do.

After Satan's attempts to stop the building of the house of the Lord, from the days of Rehum and King Artaxerxes (Cambyses) until the days of Darius, God intervenes and makes Darius sympathetic to the Jews, because "the king's heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will" (Prov 2:1). Darius issued an order for the building of the house of the Lord to continue, in which the following appeared:
1- He respected the order of the former king Cyrus, because some kings in pride neglect the orders of former kings, and even oppose them.

2- His order to Tatnai was definite and firm that the building should not be hindered, so all the soldiers and assistants of Tatnai were to keep away and not hinder the Jews from completing the temple of their God.
3- He commanded Zerubbabel the governor of the Jews and their elders to complete the house of the Lord.
4- The wisdom of Darius appears in his concern to win the love of his subjects, for permitting the Jews to build the temple of their God makes them loyal and submissive to him.

After the first item of Darius' order, the continuation of the building, the second item in this verse was the spending on this building from the money of the kingdom, so he commanded the governor beyond the river, who was Zerubbabel's superior, to give him money from the tribute collected on behalf of the king, so that Zerubbabel could complete the building. This shows Darius' great sympathy with the Jews and his awareness of their circumstances, since they were poor and needed financial help, and in this he followed the example of Cyrus the Great, who commanded that the building of the house of the Lord be paid for from the money of the kingdom.

The third item of Darius' order is his request to Tatnai to give the Jews their needs of the animals offered as burnt offerings in the temple, as well as the foodstuffs that accompany these burnt offerings when they are offered to God, such as wheat and wine... in the quantities the priests ask for according to the needs of the temple. This shows great concern on the part of Darius that the burnt offerings should continue to be offered before God, so that he says that it be given them "day by day without fail", that is, that the offering of these sacrifices should never stop.

The fourth item in Darius' order is his request to the Jews to pray always before God for him and his sons. It is useful to know about Darius that he believed in the idea of one God but did not know Him, so he agreed with the Jews in their belief in one God, since he hated the multiplicity of gods and the worship of idols. Although he did not yet believe in God, he was comforted by, and greatly esteemed, the Jews' worship of one God, so he sympathized with them greatly, as appears from this order of his.

The fifth item in Darius' order is the punishment of everyone who tries to hinder the building of the temple, and he fixed the punishment, which is very severe: that a beam be pulled out of those with which his house was built, and consequently his house would be torn down and become wreckage, ruins and a dunghill on which people's filth is thrown, and then he would be hanged on this beam, that is, the destruction of this man, the demolition of his house and the scattering of his family.

Whoever tries to fortify himself in his firm, settled house and stops the building of the house of the Lord, his house is demolished and he perishes in a horrible way, which is hanging with an instrument from his own house, while the house of the Lord is built and completed, so that his evil comes upon his own head and he perishes, but the house of God is completed.
In the end Darius showed his faith in God as a great God, able to punish His enemies, in his prayer to Him to destroy every king or people that opposes Him.
At the end of the letter containing this order, Darius signed it and commanded that this order be carried out with speed.
From this we see a miraculous divine work that took place in the heart of Darius, so that he gave this order, which contains the speedy carrying out of the following:
1- Not hindering the building of the temple and continuing to build it.
2- Spending on the needs of the temple from the money of the state.
3- Providing the animals and foodstuffs that must be offered to God in His temple.
4- Asking for prayer on his behalf and on behalf of his sons.

5- Punishing whoever opposes the building of the temple with death by hanging, the demolition of his house and its turning into a dunghill. In the order of Darius we see how God turns evil into good: if Satan stirred up the wicked against the house of the Lord, yet God, who is stronger than he, when His people drew near to Him, moved Darius, and he gave an order better and stronger than the order of Cyrus.
Do not fear the wars of the devil, but take refuge in God and ask for all you need, and He will intervene quickly and give you more than you ask or think.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: Tatnai rejoiced at the order of Darius, which came in agreement with Tatnai's feelings, and he hastened to carry out the order with all exactness. This confirms the faithfulness of Tatnai, who had first sent precisely all that he had seen in the building of the house of the Lord, and here he now hastens to carry out the orders of the king. All this was by the providence of God in completing the building of His house.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: The Jews were encouraged, so they worked quickly to complete the building, until the building of the house of the Lord was finished, and they fulfilled the word of God that He spoke on the mouth of His two prophets Haggai and Zechariah, that Zerubbabel would complete the building (Hag 1:8, Zech 4:9). In this they pleased God and also obeyed the kings of Persia, namely Cyrus and Darius and also Artaxerxes, who reigned later and in whose days Ezra and Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem, where they built the wall of the city. Ezra here, the writer of the book, mentions all the kings of Persia who encouraged and commanded the Jews to take care of building the house of the Lord and the wall of His city. The Artaxerxes mentioned here did not share in building the temple, but was mentioned in his honor, because after more than seventy years from the building of the temple he commanded the building of the wall of Jerusalem.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: The completion of the building of the temple began in the second year of Darius' reign (Ezra 3:8) and the building was finished in the sixth year of his reign, that is, it took about four years, and that was in 516 BC, on the third day of the month of Adar in the Syriac calendar, which corresponds to the month of March in the Gregorian year.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: The priests, the Levites and the rest of the people gathered to dedicate the house of the Lord, that it might become a holy place for the worship of God, and it was a great day on which they expressed their love for God by offering a large number of sacrifices: a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, in addition to twelve he-goats. We notice in these sacrifices the following:

1- Their number was much less than what Solomon offered at the dedication of the temple, and also what King Hezekiah and King Josiah offered in the celebration of the Passover (1 Kgs 8:63; 2 Chr 30:24; 35:7).

2- They offered sin offerings because they had sinned by neglecting the building of the house of the Lord, but at the building of the altar and the founding of the temple they offered only burnt offerings to please God.

3- They offered twelve he-goats for the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, although those returning from captivity were of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. This shows that those returning had become the one kingdom of Israel, offering sin offerings in love for their brethren, whether few of these tribes had returned, or some of them might return in time.

All the people rejoiced, great and small, men, women and children, at the satisfaction of God with them, because He had brought them back from captivity and granted them to build His house. But God here called them the children of the captivity, so that they would always remember their sin, because of which they were taken captive, but the mercy of God brought them back from the captivity.
We see clearly that the house of the Lord that Zerubbabel built was much less than the one that Solomon built, and here is this comparison between the two houses:

Table comparing the temple of Solomon and the temple of Zerubbabel. No. Type of comparison, Temple of Solomon, Temple of Zerubbabel. 1 Duration of its building: seven continuous years, 9 years, of which only six months was building in (1 Kgs 6:38) the reign of Cyrus, then the building stopped for four and a half years, then the building was completed in four years in the reign of Darius (Ezra 6:15). 2 Its equipment: David prepared most of it; the ruins of the temple of Solomon + the people's contributions + the gifts of the Persian state. 3 Its appearance: splendid in its beauty and greatness; very modest compared with the temple of Solomon (Hag 2:3). 4 God's coming: at its a thick cloud prevented the priests from no material form of God's coming appeared.

dedication, standing in the temple (1 Kgs 8:11). 5 The ark of the covenant: they brought it up to the temple with great glory; the presence of an ark of the covenant is not mentioned in this (1 Kgs 8:5). temple, because it was most likely lost.

6 Dedication sacrifices: 22 thousand bulls and 120 thousand sheep; 100 bulls and 200 rams and 400 lambs. 7 The kingdom: one strong kingdom comprising the twelve tribes; one weak kingdom comprising the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, and it was a province subject to the Persian kingdom. 8 The king: the greatest king in his time; there was no king, rather Israel was a province of Solomon subject to the Persian kingdom. 9 Its glory: great in its appearance; despite its modesty it was greater than the temple of Solomon because Christ entered it (Hag 2:9).

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: After the dedication of the temple they organized the service in it, by arranging the divisions of the priests and the divisions of the Levites, who took turns in the service, that is, life and worship returned to the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: The people rejoiced in the temple of God and kept their most important feast, the Passover, on the fourteenth day of the first month, after they had kept the lamb for fourteen days as the Law prescribed (Ex 12:1-10). In this every family showed its thanks to God, who freed them from the bondage of Babylon by the orders of Cyrus, then the support of Darius, as they thanked God long ago by keeping the Passover in Egypt, when He preserved their firstborn and struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues, then released them to worship Him in the wilderness of Sinai.
It is mentioned in the Old Testament that the children of Israel kept the Passover six times, which are:
1- In the land of Egypt in the days of Moses, immediately before their exodus (Ex 12:1-11).
2- In the wilderness of Sinai in the days of Moses (Num 5:9).
3- In Gilgal in the days of Joshua (Josh 5:10).
4- In the days of King Hezekiah (2 Chr 30:15).
5- In the time of King Josiah (2 Kgs 23:21).

6- In the days of Zerubbabel (Ezra 6:19). This does not mean that the Passover was not kept except these six times, but these times are mentioned because they carry a covenant with God and a renewal of the relationship with Him.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: The priests and the Levites took care to prepare for the Passover, so they purified themselves according to the Law, and consequently carried out their role in slaughtering the Passover lambs for every family of the children of Israel, and all kept the feast to the Lord.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: In this Passover there shared the Jews returning from captivity, in addition to the Jews who had been living in the land of Israel and had not gone into captivity and had mingled through pagan marriages; they separated themselves from them and purified themselves, so they were able to eat of the Passover.

The purpose of keeping the Passover here becomes clear: that they sought God, that is, they returned to Him with their hearts, leaving what they had learned in captivity from the pagans, and appeared as a people who believe in God.

entries.section: (3) The completion of the house of the Lord and its dedication

paragraphs.text: They completed the Feast of the Passover by keeping the Feast of Unleavened Bread that follows it for seven days, and they rejoiced in their worship of God who brought them back from captivity by the hand of Cyrus, and they built the house of the Lord by the order of Cyrus and Darius, who reigned over all the lands that had been subject to Assyria and Babylon. If Assyria had taken them captive long ago, now the one who reigns over Assyria, that is, Cyrus, then Darius, bring them back and build for them the temple of their God.

With the end of this chapter Ezra concludes the account of a period of time that began in 536 BC with the return of the people of God under Zerubbabel and continued until 516 BC (chs. 1-6), when the house of the Lord was built and dedicated, a period of thirty years.

Your true joy is in your worship of God in His Church and in your closet. So take care to give the best times of your life, to enjoy being in the presence of God, so that you let Him into your life and He works in you with power. Ezra and the second return to Jerusalem

1- The events mentioned in (chs. 1-6) took thirty years, from 536 to 516 BC, as we mentioned, and in this period important figures appeared, namely Zerubbabel the civil governor, Jeshua the high priest, and the two prophets Haggai and Zechariah. Then a period of 58 years passed in which Persian kings reigned, among whom we know Ahasuerus, who reigned from 486 to 465 BC, and during whose reign the events of the Book of Esther took place and the book was written during this period.

2- In the year 458 begin the events mentioned in this book from (chs. 7-10), and we see in them the second return from captivity under Ezra the priest and scribe, accompanied by 1,700 men, that is, about 8,000 persons of men, women and children. The book here mentions the details of the works of the great Ezra in Jerusalem.

3- Ezra was a contemporary of Nehemiah, who led the third return to Jerusalem in 445 BC, that is, thirteen years later, and remained governor of Jerusalem and its surroundings for about 12-13 years, and Ezra and Nehemiah were contemporaries of the prophet Malachi, who prophesied about 433 BC. The second return was in the time of King Artaxerxes, called Longimanus, who was the son of King Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther.

Now after these things: that is, after the first return of the Jews to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel, and after the building of the temple, which was completed in the reign of King Darius, and after the reign of King Ahasuerus, the husband of Esther, Artaxerxes the son of Ahasuerus became king, and his reign was from 464 to 424 BC. This was a long period, during which took place the last part of the Book of Ezra (chs. 7-10) and also the whole Book of Nehemiah.
These verses set out Ezra's priestly lineage, which reaches back to Aaron the high priest in the days of Moses. In this chain we see some important figures such as:

1- Seraiah: He was the grandfather of Ezra, not his father, and he was the high priest who was killed, among 70 of the most important men of Jerusalem, at the Babylonian attack on it, its destruction and the burning of the temple (2 Kgs 25:18-21).
2- Hilkiah: the high priest in the days of King Josiah, who found the book of the Law in the house of the Lord (2 Kgs 22:13).

3- Phinehas: the priest who killed the Israelite and the Moabite woman with whom he committed adultery, and by this the wrath of God was appeased in the face of this great immorality in the temple of God (Num 25:8).
